scope: Machine Design: complete numbered sections of supplied historical GATE/ESE solved books, selected original GATE ME and ESE Prelims through 2026, and ESE/CSE Mechanical Mains 2017–2026. Coverage is bounded by these available sources, not every examination paper ever published.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2025 · Q101
sourceIssues.issue: Statement 1 is correct. A key transmits torque between a shaft and a fitted hub, gear, pulley or coupling; the literal “between the shafts” describes a coupling, not a key alone. A power screw converts rotary motion to axial force/motion, rather than serving as an energy-storage spring. Thus only statement 1 is strictly correct, but this option is absent. Option A is the apparent intended answer if statement 2 is read as torque transfer through keyed shaft–hub coupling members. The ambiguity is retained without an automatic grade.

sourceIssues.title: GATE ME 2007 · Set 1 · Q54
sourceIssues.issue: The printed data and end-condition wording do not produce an exact listed Euler result. I=pi×20^4/64=7853.98 mm^4 and pi²EI/L²=31.6385 kN. If “guided at the piston” is treated as laterally fixed with zero rotation and the other end hinged, exact effective-length factor K≈0.699 gives FOS≈6.48. Using the older approximate K=0.75 gives FOS=5.6246, matching intended option C. A laterally sliding guided support gives a different boundary-value problem. Because no approximation is specified, the conditional result is shown and the item is excluded from automatic grading.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2023 · Q105
sourceIssues.issue: With a total clamping load of 4000 N shared equally by three bolts, each bolt carries 1333.33 N and requires tensile area At=1333.33/800=1.66667 mm². None of the choices gives this per-bolt area. Option C, 5 mm², is the required combined area of all three bolts, or the per-bolt area only if each bolt carries 4000 N. The question asks for the area “for the bolt”; this ambiguity is explained rather than forcing an incorrect grade.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2013 | Machine Design Book Q3.87
sourceIssues.issue: The supplied key is A (pitting). Removal of surface particles/flakes from a rolling-contact raceway is also termed spalling (C); pitting and spalling describe related surface-fatigue damage and this wording does not distinguish their scale. Compare the terms and the printed key; this item is excluded from automatic scoring.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2016 | Machine Design Book Q3.103
sourceIssues.issue: Sommerfeld number S=(mu n/p)(r/c)^2. Here p=W/(LD)=3672/(0.1×0.05)=734400 Pa, n=500/60 s−1, r/c=D/(diametral clearance)=0.05/0.0001=500. Thus S=0.170207, dimensionless. The printed choices do not match; a dimensional or exponent error is present in the source.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2012 | Machine Design Book Q6.26
sourceIssues.issue: Both square and Acme threads can transmit power in either direction. The identical source appearances print A (Acme, 1999) and B (square, 2012). B is the conventional textbook selection, but the statement does not uniquely exclude A. This item is excluded from automatic scoring.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2023 · Q82
sourceIssues.issue: The intended textbook combination appears to be 1 and 3 (option C), with Vitallium correctly rejected because it is cobalt-based rather than vanadium-based. However statement 1 calls both Discalloy and Incoloy nickel-based while describing iron–nickel alloys. Incoloy is a family with varying Fe/Ni proportions (for example alloy 800 has Fe at least 39.5% and Ni 30–35%); a blanket base-metal classification is imprecise. No unqualified automatic grade is imposed on this inconsistent wording. Reference: Special Metals INCOLOY alloy 800 technical bulletin, https://www.specialmetals.com/documents/technical-bulletins/incoloy/incoloy-alloy-800.pdf .

visualReview.method: All initial question crops inspected on contact sheets; focused source-page checks for shared statements, split questions and diagrams. Rebuilt ESE column widths from complete text extents and reviewed repaired contact sheets; reconstructed historical shared-data blocks and original GATE boundaries.
repairs: Complete book question boundaries instead of truncating last option lines
GATE 2008 linked bolt statements and 2013 riveted-joint common data
Historical gear and band-brake common data
Three recovered GATE 2020 questions with official keys
Removal of appended answer-key pages and extraneous continuation panels
visualReview.sourceLimit: A few historical ESE pages have faint, creased or damaged source lettering; cropping cannot restore absent pixels.

limitations: Written answers are independent self-review references, not official UPSC marking schemes.
Ambiguous or inconsistent source questions have explained conditional references and are excluded from automatic scoring.
Historical book keys are attributed to the supplied books, not relabelled as official examination keys.
Machine Design shares foundational mechanics and gear-design questions with SOM/TOM; their earlier subject identities remain intact.
No unsupported claim is made that the supplied PDFs contain every historical paper.
